title: 1965 AHSME Problem 21
statement:
It is possible to choose \(x\gt\dfrac23\) in such a way that the value of

\[ \log_{10}(x^2+3)-2\log_{10}x \]

is:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
smaller than any positive number that might be
specified

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: greater than any positive number that might be specified

solutions.text:
The expression is \[ \begin{gathered} \log_{10}\left(\frac{x^2+3}{x^2}\right)\\ =\log_{10}\left(1+\frac3{x^2}\right). \end{gathered} \] It is always positive, but tends to \(0\) as \(x\) grows. Therefore it can be made smaller than any specified positive number.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
